We have mass spec, proton NMR, and we guessed a structure Brc1ccc(OCC)cc1 (para-bromo phenoxy ethyl?). The formula C8H9BrO matches mass? Let's compute monoisotopic mass: C8=96.000, H9=9.070, Br=78.9183 (79Br) or 80.916? Actually Br isotopes 79 (78.9183) and 81 (80.9163). O=15.9949. Sum = 96+9.07+78.918+15.995=199.983 ~ 199.98. Observed m/z 198.99966 (likely M+? maybe M+? The mass spec shows peaks at 199, 200, 201, etc. The base peak at 199 (intensity 100). That matches molecular ion M+? For C8H9BrO, M+ would be 199 (79Br) or 201 (81Br). Indeed we see peaks at 199 (100) and 201 (97.6) which correspond to isotopic pattern of Br (approx 1:1). Also peaks at 200 (9) and 202 (8.9) correspond to M+1 isotopes (C13 etc). So mass spec matches C8H9BrO.

Proton NMR: 2.62 (t, 2H), 2.77 (t, 2H) suggests ethoxy chain O-CH2-CH2- attached to aromatic? Actually OCH2CH2 attached to aromatic: O-CH2-CH2-? The O-CH2 (adjacent to O) appears around 3.5-4.0 ppm, not 2.6. But maybe it's phenoxy ethyl bromide? Wait we have Br on aromatic, OCH2CH3? The NMR shows two triplets each 2H at 2.62 and 2.77, typical for -CH2-CH2- attached to aromatic (Ar-CH2-CH2-X). For phenoxy ethyl (Ar-O-CH2-CH3) you'd have O-CH2 at ~3.8 ppm, not 2.6. So maybe it's Br-CH2-CH2-O-Ph? That would give CH2 next to Br ~3.4? Actually CH2 attached to Br appears ~3.4-3.5. CH2 attached to O appears ~3.5-4.0. Both similar. But we have aromatic protons: 7.18 ddd 2H, 7.36 ddd 2H typical para-disubstituted benzene (AA'BB') pattern. So aromatic ring has two substituents para to each other: one Br, one OCH2CH2? So structure is p-bromo phenoxy ethyl? Actually OCH2CH2 attached to aromatic via O (phenoxy). So the substituents are Br and OCH2CH2 (ethoxy). That matches our SMILES Brc1ccc(OCC)cc1 (para-bromo phenoxy ethyl). The OCH2CH2 group: O-CH2-CH3? Wait OCH2CH2 is -O-CH2-CH3? Actually OCH2CH2 is -O-CH2-CH3? No, OCH2CH2 is -O-CH2-CH2-? The SMILES O C C means O-CH2-CH3 (ethoxy). So OCH2CH3 attached to aromatic via O. That gives O-CH2 (attached to O) at ~3.8 ppm, not 2.6. But we have two triplets each 2H, not a quartet. Ethoxy would give CH3 quartet and CH2 triplet. So not ethoxy. OCH2CH2 (hydroxyethyl) attached via O to aromatic: -O-CH2-CH2-? The terminal CH2 would be attached to something else? Actually OCH2CH2- (hydroxyethyl) would have O-CH2 (attached to O) ~3.5 ppm, CH2 attached to something else maybe H? Not matching.

Our NMR shows two triplets each 2H, typical for -CH2-CH2- where each CH2 is adjacent to another CH2 (both triplets). So the chain is -CH2-CH2- attached to aromatic at one end and to Br at the other? But Br is on aromatic, not chain. So maybe the chain is -CH2-CH2- attached to O (ether) and to aromatic? Actually O-CH2-CH2- attached to aromatic via O gives O-CH2 (triplet) and CH2 attached to something else (maybe CH2 attached to O? both adjacent to each other, both triplets). Yes O-CH2-CH2-Ph (phenoxy ethyl) would have O-CH2 (adjacent to CH2) and CH2 attached to aromatic (via O? Actually the chain is O-CH2-CH2-Ph? Wait phenoxy ethyl is Ph-O-CH2-CH3. That's O-CH2 attached to aromatic O, not CH2 attached to aromatic. So the CH2 attached to aromatic is not present.

Our SMILES Brc1ccc(OCC)cc1 is para-bromo phenoxy ethyl (Ph-O-CH2-CH3). That would give O-CH2 (triplet) and CH3 (quartet). Not matching.

Thus our guess may be wrong. Let's consider alternative: p-bromo phenyl-CH2-CH2-OH? That would be Br-Ph-CH2-CH2-OH (bromo phenethyl alcohol). SMILES: Brc1ccc(CCO)cc1. That would have CH2 next to aromatic (around 2.7) triplet, CH2 next to OH (around 3.5) triplet. That matches two triplets 2.62 and 2.77 (both similar). Aromatic protons same pattern. Formula: C8H9BrO? Let's compute: C8H9BrO is same as before. Brc1ccc(CCO)cc1 has C8H9BrO? Count: phenyl (C6H4) plus Br substituent (Br) plus CH2-CH2-OH (C2H5O). Total C8 H9? C6+2=8, H4+5=9, O1, Br1. Yes matches formula. So this is likely correct: p-bromo phenethyl alcohol.

Mass spec matches. NMR: aromatic AA'BB' pattern, two triplets for CH2-CH2. Good.

Thus final SMILES: Brc1ccc(CCO)cc1 (para-bromo phenethyl alcohol). Need to ensure correct orientation: Br at position 1, chain at para (position 4). SMILES can be "Brc1ccc(cc1)CCO"? Actually "Brc1ccc(CCO)cc1" is fine.

We should validate SMILES.
